datePresets.lastMonth: A rolling 30-day window ending today — not the previous calendar month (see 'Prior Month').
datePresets.priorMonth: The previous full calendar month (e.g. all of September if today is in October), unlike the rolling 'Last Month'.
datePresets.priorQuarter: The previous full calendar quarter, as opposed to a rolling 3-month window.
datePresets.prior6Months: The 6 full calendar months before the current one, not including the current month.
datePresets.priorYear: Jan 1 to Dec 31 of the previous calendar year, as opposed to a rolling 12-month window.

actions.exportHcmask: Exports the generated mask list as a .hcmask file (one hashcat mask per line) for use with hashcat's mask-attack mode.
actions.exportInternalPdf: Full report PDF including recovered plaintext passwords — for internal use only, not for sharing with the client.
actions.exportExternalPdf: Client-safe PDF with cracked passwords and other sensitive data redacted, suitable to share externally.

sections.maskAnalysis: Breaks cracked passwords down by their hashcat mask pattern (e.g. ?u?l?l?l?d?d); this is descriptive analysis, not an attack input.
sections.domainBreakdown: Breakdown by the Windows/AD domain extracted from the hashes, not a web domain.
sections.positionalAnalysis: Analyzes which character types (upper/lower/digit/special) appear at each position within cracked passwords.
sections.baseWords: The underlying dictionary word in a password after stripping leet-speak, digits, and case variation (e.g. 'P@ssw0rd123' -> 'password').

columns.domain: The Windows/AD domain extracted from the hash, not a web domain.
columns.hashlistCount: Number of different hashlists this password/hash was found in.
columns.matchPercentage: Percentage of LM-cracked users whose recovered case pattern matches this mask.
columns.speedLevel: A cracking-speed scenario expressed as a percentage of this hashlist's benchmarked hash rate, used for time-to-crack estimates.
columns.usersHashlistCount: Number of distinct users, together with the number of distinct hashlists, this password was found in.
columns.estimatedKeyspace: Estimated hashcat keyspace (number of candidate passwords) these generated masks will cover.
columns.firstHalf: LM hashes split a password into two independent 7-character halves cracked separately; this is the first half's (characters 1-7) status.
columns.secondHalf: LM hashes split a password into two independent 7-character halves cracked separately; this is the second half's (characters 8-14) status.

labels.bothCracked: Both this user's LM and NTLM hashes were cracked.
labels.ntlmOnly: Only this user's NTLM hash was cracked; the linked LM hash was not.
labels.lmOnly: Only this user's LM hash was cracked; the linked NTLM hash was not.
labels.neitherCracked: Neither this user's LM nor NTLM hash was cracked.
labels.firstHalfOnly: Only the first 7-character half of this LM password was cracked.
labels.secondHalfOnly: Only the second 7-character half (characters 8-14) of this LM password was cracked.
labels.totalPartial: Total count of LM passwords where only one of the two 7-character halves was cracked.

descriptions.lmDerivable: Indicates this NTLM case-variation can be derived/confirmed from the already-cracked LM pattern.
descriptions.ntlmUnknown: Indicates the corresponding NTLM hash hasn't been cracked yet, even though the LM half was.

bloodhound.kerberoastable: 'Kerberoastable' accounts have Kerberos service-ticket hashes that can be cracked offline (a known AD attack technique).
bloodhound.asrepRoastable: 'AS-REP Roastable' accounts don't require Kerberos pre-authentication, so their hashes can be cracked offline (AS-REP roasting).
bloodhound.adminCount: 'AdminCount (AdminSDHolder)' flags accounts AD still marks as protected/privileged, even if no longer in a privileged group.
bloodhound.dcsyncCapable: 'DCSync-capable' accounts can impersonate a domain controller to dump every password hash in the domain.
bloodhound.localAdminBlast: 'Blast radius' = how many machines this cracked account has local-admin rights on (its lateral-movement reach).
bloodhound.crackedTierZero: 'Tier-0' is BloodHound's label for the domain's most privileged assets (e.g. domain controllers, domain admins).
bloodhound.hops: Number of steps in the BloodHound attack-path graph needed to reach Domain Admin from this account.
bloodhound.daChip: 'DA' = Domain Admin; {{n}} is the count of cracked accounts holding that role.
bloodhound.inDomain: '(dump)' means this figure comes from the uploaded BloodHound collection file, not from cracking results.
